children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and also to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,

children.text: devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva tato jayam udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: and also to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, thereafter one should proclaim victory.
O you whose hair-ends are like heated gold, whose eyes blaze like fire,
O divine lion, whose claws touch more powerfully than the thunderbolt, homage to you.
May the tips of <s>Narasiṃha</s>'s claws and tail protect you,
reddened with the muddy blood from the field of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>'s breast.
All the sages dwelling on <s>Himavat</s>, who had reached the far shore of the Vedas,
great-souled knowers of the three times, and those dwelling in <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>,
those devoted to the <s>Arbuda</s> forest, the dwellers in the <s>Puṣkara</s> forest,

children.text: mahendrādriratā ye ca ye ca vindhyanivāsinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those attached to <s>Mahendra</s> mountain, and those dwelling in the <s>Vindhya</s>,
those devoted to <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> and those dwelling in <s>Daṇḍakāraṇya</s>,
those devoted to <s>Śrīśaila</s> and those dwelling at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>,

children.text: kaumāraparvate ye ca ye ca pampānivāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: those on <s>Kumāra</s> mountain and those dwelling at <s>Pampā</s>,

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ saśiṣyā munayo 'malāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these and many other stainless sages, together with their disciples,

children.text: māghamāse prayāgaṃ tu snātuṃ tīrthaṃ samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: came together in the month of <s>Māgha</s> to bathe at the tīrtha (sacred ford) of <s>Prayāga</s>.

children.text: tatra snātvā yathānyāyaṃ kṛtvā karma japādikam ||
children.translated_text: There, having bathed according to rule and performed rites such as recitation,

children.text: natvā tu mādhavaṃ devaṃ kṛtvā ca pitṛtarpaṇam
children.translated_text: having bowed to the god <s>Mādhava</s> and made offerings of water to the ancestors,
they saw <s>Bharadvāja</s> there, dwelling at that holy tīrtha.

children.text: taṃ pūjayitvā vidhivat tenaiva ca supūjitāḥ
children.translated_text: After honoring him according to rule, and being well honored by him in return,
on various seats, on bull-hides and the like, each in proper order,
given by <s>Bharadvāja</s>, those rich in austerity sat down.
All of them, devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then spoke among themselves of sacred stories.
At the end of those stories among those sages of disciplined minds,
there came there the very brilliant <s>Sūta</s>, a man of great understanding,
<s>Vyāsa</s>'s disciple, a knower of the Purāṇas, known by the name <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: tān praṇamya yathānyāyaṃ sa ca taiś cābhipūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He bowed to them according to rule, and he too was honored by them.
Then he sat down suitably, with <s>Bharadvāja</s>'s approval.
Thereupon, when <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>'s disciple, was seated comfortably,

children.text: sa papraccha bharadvājo munīnām agratas tadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bharadvāja</s> questioned him then in the presence of the sages.
<s>Bharadvāja</s> said:
At the great sacrifice of <s>Śaunaka</s>, the compendium called the <s>Vārāha</s>,

children.text: tvattaḥ śrutā purā sūta etair asmābhir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, was formerly heard from you by these men and by us as well.
Now I wish to hear from you the Purāṇic compendium called <s>Nārasiṃha</s>,

children.text: śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ sūta śrotukāmā ime sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>; these men too stand here desiring to hear it.

children.text: atas tvāṃ paripṛcchāmi praśnam etaṃ mahāmune
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask you this question, great sage,

children.text: ṛṣīṇām agrataḥ sūta prātar hy eṣāṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, in the presence of the seers, early in the morning, before these great souls:

children.text: kuta etat samutpannaṃ kena vā paripālyate
children.translated_text: From what has this arisen, and by whom is it protected?

children.text: kasmin vā layam abhyeti jagad etaccarācaram ||
children.translated_text: And into what does this whole world, moving and unmoving, enter at dissolution?

children.text: kiṃ pramāṇaṃ ca vai bhūmer nṛsiṃhaḥ kena tuṣyati
children.translated_text: What is the measure of the earth, and by what action is <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> pleased?

children.text: karmaṇā tu mahābhāga tan me brūhi mahāmate ||
children.translated_text: Greatly fortunate one, man of great understanding, tell me that.

children.text: kathaṃ ca sṛṣṭer ādiḥ syād avasānaṃ kathaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: How is there a beginning of creation, and how does its end come about?

children.text: kathaṃ yugasya gaṇanā kiṃ vā syāt tu caturyugam ||
children.translated_text: How is the age reckoned, and what is a caturyuga (cycle of four ages)?

children.text: ko vā viśeṣas teṣvatra kā vāvasthā kalau yuge
children.translated_text: What distinction is there among them here, and what condition prevails in the Kali age?
How is the god <s>Narasiṃha</s> worshiped even by non-human beings?

children.text: kṣetrāṇi kāni puṇyāni ke ca puṇyāḥ śiloccayāḥ
children.translated_text: Which regions are holy, and which rocky mountains are holy?

children.text: nadyaś ca kāḥ parāḥ puṇyā nṛṇāṃ pāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And which supreme, holy, auspicious rivers remove the sins of men?

children.text: devādīnāṃ kathaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ manor manvantarasya tu
children.translated_text: How is the creation of the gods and others, and of <s>Manu</s>'s manvantara (age of a Manu),

children.text: tathā vidyādharādīnāṃ sṛṣṭir ādau kathaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise how at the beginning does the creation of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> and others take place?

children.text: yajvānaḥ ke ca rājānaḥ ke ca siddhiṃ parāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Who are the sacrificing kings, and who have attained supreme perfection?
Tell all this, greatly fortunate one, in proper order.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
By <s>Vyāsa</s>'s favor I know the Purāṇas, O you rich in austerity.
Having bowed to him, I shall expound the <s>Nārasiṃha</s> Purāṇa.

children.text: pārāśaryaṃ paramapuruṣaṃ viśvadevaikayoniṃ vidyāvantaṃ vipulamatidaṃ vedavedāṅgavedyam
children.translated_text: I always bow to <s>Vedavyāsa</s>, son of <s>Parāśara</s>, the supreme person, the single womb of all the gods, learned, giver of vast understanding, knowable through the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

children.text: śaśvacchāntaṃ śamitaviṣayaṃ śuddhatejoviśālam vedavyāsaṃ vigataśamalaṃ sarvadāhaṃ namāmi ||
children.translated_text: ever peaceful, with the senses subdued, broad with pure radiance, free from stain.
Homage to that blessed <s>Vyāsa</s> of immeasurable brilliance,
by whose favor I shall tell this account of <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: sunirṇīto mahān praśnas tvayā yaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: The great question that you have stated has been very well determined.
Without the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by whom could it possibly be spoken?
Nevertheless, by the grace of <s>Narasiṃha</s> himself, now for you
I shall expound this very holy matter. <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, listen to me.

children.text: śṛṇvantu munayaḥ sarve saśiṣyās tv atra ye sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Let all the sages who are present here together with their disciples listen.
I shall expound the Purāṇa of <s>Narasiṃha</s> as it truly is.
From <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> all this, moving and unmoving, has arisen.
By him alone all is protected, through forms beginning with <s>Narasiṃha</s>.
And likewise, at the end, it dissolves into <s>Hari</s>, whose nature is light.

children.text: yathaiva devaḥ sṛjati tathā vakṣyāmi tacchṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Just how the god creates, that I shall tell; listen to it.

children.text: purāṇānāṃ hi sarveṣām ayaṃ sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: For all the Purāṇas this is remembered as common:

children.text: śloko yas taṃ mune śrutvā niḥśeṣaṃ tvaṃ tataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: when you have heard that verse, sage, then hear the whole matter completely.

children.text: sargaś ca pratisargaś ca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca
children.translated_text: Creation, re-creation, lineage, the manvantaras,
and the accounts following the lineages: a Purāṇa has five marks.
Primary creation, secondary creation, lineage, the manvantaras,
and the accounts following the lineages: these I shall state in summary.

children.text: ādisargo mahāṃs tāvat kathayiṣyāmi vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: First I shall indeed tell the great primary creation, O twice-born ones,

children.text: yasmād ārabhya devānāṃ rājñāṃ caritam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: from which, beginning onward, the history of gods and kings
is known, together with its secret meaning and the eternal supreme self.

children.text: prāk sṛṣṭeḥ pralayād ūrdhvaṃ nāsīt kiṃcid dvijottama ||
children.translated_text: Before creation, after the dissolution, there was nothing at all, best of twice-born men.
There was only that which is called Brahman, luminous and the cause of all.
It is eternal, stainless, peaceful, without qualities, and ever pure.
It is a clear ocean of bliss, which those who seek liberation long for.
It is omniscient because its nature is knowledge, endless, unborn, and imperishable.
But when the time for creation had arrived, that lord of knowers, having known it,

children.text: antarlīnaṃ vikāraṃ ca tat sraṣṭum upacakrame ||
children.translated_text: began to create the modification that lay hidden within.

children.text: tasmāt pradhānam udbhūtaṃ tataś cāpi mahān abhūt
children.translated_text: From that arose <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), and from it <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) came forth.

children.text: sāttviko rājasaś caiva tāmasaś ca tridhā mahān ||
children.translated_text: That <s>mahat</s> is threefold: sāttvika, rājasa, and tāmasa.

children.text: vaikārikas taijasaś ca bhūtādiś caiva tāmasaḥ
children.translated_text: The vaikārika, the taijasa, and the tāmasa called bhūtādi:
this threefold <s>ahaṃkāra</s> arose from the <s>mahat-tattva</s>.

children.text: yathā pradhānaṃ hi mahān mahatā sa tathāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as <s>mahat</s> is enveloped by <s>pradhāna</s>, so that in turn is enveloped by <s>mahat</s>.
Then bhūtādi, undergoing transformation, produced the subtle element of sound.
From the subtle element of sound it created ether, whose mark is sound.
Bhūtādi then enveloped ether, which possessed sound alone.

children.text: ākāśas tu vikurvāṇaḥ sparśamātraṃ sasarja ha
children.translated_text: Ether, undergoing transformation, created the subtle element of touch.

children.text: balavān abhavad vāyus tasya sparśo guṇo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wind became powerful; touch is held to be its quality.
The subtle element of sound, namely ether, then enveloped the subtle element of touch.

children.text: tato vāyur vikurvāṇo rūpamātraṃ sasarja ha ||
children.translated_text: Then wind, undergoing transformation, created the subtle element of form.

children.text: jyotir utpadyate vāyos tad rūpaguṇam ucyate
children.translated_text: From wind fire comes into being; form is said to be its quality.

children.text: sparśamātraṃ tu vai vāyū rūpamātraṃ samāvṛṇot ||
children.translated_text: Wind, possessing touch alone, enveloped the subtle element of form.

children.text: jyotiś cāpi vikurvāṇaṃ rasamātraṃ sasarja ha
children.translated_text: Fire too, undergoing transformation, created the subtle element of taste.
From that arise the waters, and they are the supports of taste.
The waters, possessing the subtle element of taste, enveloped the subtle element of form.
And the waters, undergoing transformation, created the subtle element of smell.
From that was born this earth, superior in the qualities of all beings.

children.text: saṃghāto jāyate tasmāt tasya gandhaguṇo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that a solid aggregate arises; smell is held to be its quality.

children.text: tasmiṃs tasmiṃs tu tanmātrā tena tanmātratā smṛtā
children.translated_text: In each of these there is that particular subtle element; therefore its state as a subtle element is remembered.
The subtle elements are undifferentiated; the differentiated forms are other, proceeding in order.
This creation of the elements and subtle elements from tāmasa <s>ahaṃkāra</s>

children.text: kīrtitas te samāsena bharadvāja mayā tava ||
children.translated_text: has been recounted to you briefly by me, <s>Bharadvāja</s>.
They say the senses are taijasa, and the ten deities are vaikārika.

children.text: ekādaśaṃ manaś cātra kīrtitaṃ tatra cintakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the eleventh here, the mind is mentioned there by the thinkers.
Here there are five cognitive senses and five organs of action.

children.text: tāni vakṣyāmi teṣāṃ ca karmāṇi kulapāvana ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you these and their functions, purifier of your family.

children.text: śravaṇe ca dṛśau jihvā nāsikā tvak ca pañcamī
children.translated_text: Hearing, the two eyes, the tongue, the nose, and skin as the fifth:
these five, joined with understanding, serve for the knowledge of sound and the other objects.
The anus, genitals, hands, feet, and speech as the fifth, <s>Bharadvāja</s>:

children.text: visargānandaśilpī ca gatyuktī karma tat smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: excretion, pleasure, making, movement, and utterance are remembered as their functions.
Ether, wind, fire, water, and likewise earth,
are joined, O learned one, with the qualities beginning with sound, each later one adding to the former.

children.text: nānāvīryāḥ pṛthagbhūtās tatas te saṃhatiṃ vinā
children.translated_text: Though of various powers and separately arisen, without combination
they could not create progeny, since they had not wholly come together.
Having assembled into mutual conjunction, through reciprocal dependence,
and having completely attained unity, marked as a single aggregate,
because they were presided over by <s>puruṣa</s> and aided by <s>pradhāna</s>,

children.text: mahadādyā viśeṣāntās tv aṇḍam utpādayanti te ||
children.translated_text: those principles, from <s>mahat</s> down to the differentiated forms, produced the egg.

children.text: tat krameṇa vivṛddhaṃ tu jalabudbudavat sthitam
children.translated_text: It gradually increased and remained like a bubble in water.
From the elements, great-minded one, came the great egg, resting in the waters.
It was natural, the unsurpassed abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose form is Brahman.
There that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord and master of the universe, whose nature is unmanifest,
took on the form of <s>Brahmā</s> and remained there himself.

children.text: merur ulbam abhūt tasya jarāyuś ca mahīdharāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s> became its caul, and the mountains its fetal membrane.
The oceans became the embryonic water of that great being.
The mountains, continents, oceans, and the collection of worlds with the luminaries
all came to be within that egg, together with gods, asuras, and humans.

children.text: rajoguṇayuto devaḥ svayam eva hariḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: The supreme god <s>Hari</s> himself, joined with the quality of rajas,
assumes the form of <s>Brahmā</s> and proceeds in the creation of the world.

children.text: sṛṣṭaṃ ca pāty anuyugaṃ yāvat kalpavikalpanā
children.translated_text: And, once it has been created, he protects it age after age, as long as the succession of kalpas lasts.
In the form of <s>Narasiṃha</s> and the like, and in the form of <s>Rudra</s>, he destroys it.

children.text: brāhmeṇa rūpeṇa sṛjaty ananto jagat samastaṃ paripātum icchan
children.translated_text: In the Brahmā-form, the endless one creates the whole world, wishing to protect it.

children.text: rāmādirūpaṃ sa tu gṛhya pāti bhūtvātha rudraḥ prakaroti nāśam ||
children.translated_text: Taking the form of <s>Rāma</s> and others, he protects it; then, becoming <s>Rudra</s>, he brings about destruction.
